questions.q: What happens when you register a model under a name that already exists in the Azure ML registry?
options: The old model is overwritten and deleted
The registration fails
The registry increments the version number
A new workspace is created
questions.explain: Per Microsoft Learn, models are identified by name and version, and registering again with the same name increments the version.

questions.q: Which properties of a registered model version can be updated in place, according to the docs?
options: Only the description and tags
Only the model files
The type and the path
Everything except the name
questions.explain: For models, only description and tags are mutable. To change anything else, such as the files, create a new version.

questions.q: Why is registering from an MLflow runs:/<run-id>/... path useful?
options: It makes the model train faster
It skips the registry entirely
It converts the model to ONNX
It records lineage between the registered model and the run that produced it
questions.explain: The docs say the runs: URI format establishes lineage between the registered model and its source run, so you can trace back the training metrics and code.

questions.q: What does archiving a model do?
options: Deletes it permanently
Hides it from default list queries while you can still reference and use it
Blocks every deployment that uses it
Moves it to another region
questions.explain: Archiving hides a model from default list queries, but you can continue to reference and use an archived model in workflows.

questions.q: Why would a team use an Azure ML registry instead of only a workspace?
options: Registries are free and workspaces are not
To share models across dev, test and production workspaces, even in different subscriptions or regions
To avoid versioning models
Registries train the models for you
questions.explain: Registries decouple models, environments, components and data assets from any single workspace so they can be developed in one place and deployed to endpoints in others.
